name: linear-search
description: Same kind of linear problem, smaller (200 actions in R^10, 5 instances, 4 runs each). LinUCB and LinTS with theoretical values, then with the best alpha and lambda found on other seeds.

policies.label: LinUCB
notes: lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)

policies.label: LinUCB searched
notes: lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)

policies.label: LinTS searched
notes: lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)

notices.title: Default hyperparameters
notices.text: alpha=1 for LinUCB and LinTS. These are the values of the papers. They are safe in theory but often explore too much. To tune them, run a grid search: param_grid=True ("param_grid": true in a config file). Or set them yourself, e.g. LinUCB(alpha=0.1).

notices.title: Grid search
notices.text: LinUCB searched and LinTS searched: 18 combinations tried before the reported runs (2 run(s) each, other seeds). The best final regret is kept. These values fit this problem only.

notices.title: Not stored
notices.text: Pseudo-regret ("pseudo_regret"), action of every step ("actions"), peak memory (measure_memory=True). The charts cannot show them. The brackets say how to store each one: a quoted name goes in track ("track": [...] in a config file).

notices.title: One point every 10 steps
notices.text: Curves keep one point every 10 steps, plus the last step. Between two points, the line is drawn, not measured. You set log_interval=10. log_interval=1 keeps every step (larger files).

notices.title: Parallel runs
notices.text: n_jobs=4: runs in parallel, one BLAS thread each. Compare CPU times only between runs with the same n_jobs.
